chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, from some of our companions, who said:

Al-Rabīʿ came to Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr while he was the caliph and was in ṭawāf, and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, so-and-so, your mawlā, died last night, and so-and-so, your mawlā, cut off his head after his death.” He said: So he became enraged and angry. He then said to Ibn Shubrumah, Ibn Abī Laylā, and a number of judges and fuqahāʾ: “What do you say regarding this?” Each one said: “We have nothing on this matter.” He continued repeating the question and saying: “Should I kill him or not?” They said: “We have nothing on this matter.” Then some of them said to him: “A man has just arrived now; if anyone has an answer to this, then he has the answer to it, and he is Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he has entered the saʿy.” So he said to al-Rabīʿ: “Go to him and say to him: Were it not for our knowing of the engagement you are in, we would have asked you to come to us; but answer us regarding such-and-such.”

He said: So al-Rabīʿ came to him while he was on al-Marwah and conveyed the message to him. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “You can see the occupation I am engaged in, and before you are the fuqahāʾ and the scholars, so ask them.” He said to him: “He has asked them, but they had nothing on it.” He said: So he repeated it to him, and said: “I ask you only that you answer us regarding it, for the people have nothing on this matter.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him: “Until I finish what I am engaged in.” He said: Then when he had finished, he came and sat at the side of al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and said to al-Rabīʿ: “Go and say to him: ‘One hundred dinars are due upon him.’” He said: So he conveyed that to him, and they said to him: “Then ask him how one hundred dinars became due upon him.”

So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “For the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the ʿalaqah twenty, for the muḍghah twenty, for the bone twenty, and for the flesh twenty: ‘ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ’; and this dead person is in his rank like that before the spirit is breathed into him in his mother’s womb, as a fetus.”

He said: So he returned to him and informed him of the answer, and that impressed them. They said: “Go back to him and ask him: the dinars, for whom are they? For his heirs or not?” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “His heirs have no share in them. Rather, this is something that came to belong to him in his body after his death; hajj may be performed with it on his behalf, or charity may be given with it on his behalf, or it may be placed in a way among the ways of الخير.” He said: The man claimed that they sent the messenger back to him, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام answered thirty-six issues regarding it, but the man did not retain except the extent of this answer.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting off the head of a dead person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report narrates a legal question presented to Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام about cutting off the head of a dead person after death. The Imam عليه السلام rules that one hundred dinars are due, analogizing the dead body to the stages before the soul is breathed into the fetus, and clarifies that this payment does not go to the heirs but is spent on acts of good on behalf of the deceased.
